citation.title: Populating cellular metamaterials on the extrema of attainable elasticity through neuroevolution
citation.authors: Maohua Yan; Ruicheng Wang; Ke Liu
citation.venue: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 440, 117950
citation.version_coded: arXiv preprint PDF; journal version not accessible as an open full text

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: The authors present neuroevolution as a more efficient way than gradient topology optimization to survey broad metamaterial property spaces and identify attainable elastic-property bounds.
claim.key_phrase: not efficient tools for surveying the vast design space
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No runtime or speed-up for the proposed method against the cited classical optimizer is reported. The introduction's thousands-fold statement describes earlier VAE studies, not this method.
claim.alternatives: Section 3.3/Figure 11: after 800 neuroevolution iterations, elastic-property trends agree with cited topology-optimization results [5], while the proposed front is described as denser. Section 3.5 claims intermediate designs are retained without extra computation.

baseline.classical_method: Topology-optimization-driven metamaterial design in cited reference [5] (Section 3.3)
baseline.hardware_ml: Alibaba Cloud AMD EPYC 7H12 64-core processors, 256 processors total, 2.60 GHz, 503 GiB DDR4 RAM; no GPU (Section 3 opening)
baseline.problem_size: 2D periodic metamaterial unit cells; element count not stated for the cited comparison (Section 3)
baseline.training_time: not stated; CPPNs evolve during each optimization rather than offline training
baseline.data_generation_cost: not stated; no prior training data are used (Section 4)
baseline.quality_metric: Effective elasticity tensor and derived Young's modulus/Poisson ratio from FE computational homogenization (Section 3, Appendix A)
baseline.quality_gap: Section 3.3 reports property trends consistent with reference [5] and a denser Pareto-front distribution, without a numeric matched quality gap

R1.evidence: Abstract claims more efficient survey; Section 3.3 compares property-space coverage with the cited topology-optimization study, but no equal-quality, equal-time or equal-FE-evaluation comparison is supplied.

R2.evidence: Section 3.3 cites an earlier topology-optimization result without timings or solver information; none of R2(a)-(e) can be established.

R3.evidence: Sections 2 and 4 describe CPPNs evolving during each design search with no offline training; optimization cost belongs to R1/R2.

R4.evidence: Section 2 and Appendix A evaluate returned cell properties by FE homogenization and Section 2.2.3 handles disconnected designs as constraint violations, but no aggregate infeasibility rate for outputs is reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: 4 property-space/symmetry families: isotropic, tetragonal, orthotropic and anisotropic (Sections 3.1-3.4)

notes: Section 3.3 compares the produced Pareto front with a classical topology-optimization study's reported result, so the paper has a cited classical result beyond its background motivation. The primary abstract claim concerns efficiency of design-space surveying; no paired runtime is given.
